punapāpajjasī.meaning_2: you will come to grief again; you will fall into misfortune again
punapāpajjasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of puna + āpajjasi (present 2nd singular of āpajjati, 'to undergo, incur, fall into'). In the text it stands at the start of a verse.
punapāpajjasī.translation_2: You will come to grief again, friend, for your moral conduct is just like that.

saṅkitabbāni.meaning_2: to be suspected; to be doubted; to be feared
saṅkitabbāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Potential participle used in the neuter plural (saṅkitabbāni) in the verse: 'saṅkeyya saṅkitabbāni'. The form is passive, 'things to be suspected'. The PEU entry is doubtful; √saṅk (doubt, suspect) fits the context.
saṅkitabbāni.translation_2: 44. One should suspect what is to be suspected; one should guard against the danger yet to come;

sīliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. Possibly related to sīla; PEU suggests 'virtuous person', but the context supports 'virtue/conduct'.
sīliyaṃ.translation_2: 84. Therefore, exert your effort, overcome your bad habits;

cīti.meaning_2: scheming; plotting; this way and that; (reduplicated) iti cīti
cīti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Echo-word of iti in the phrase iti cīti ca, expressing evasive scheming talk ('this way and that'). Treated as an indeclinable; possibly an onomatopoeic reduplication of iti.
cīti.example_2: Yañcetaṃ iti cīti ca, etampi viditaṃ mayā.
cīti.translation_2: And this scheming of yours—this too is known to me.

māgamāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the prohibitive particle mā with the 2nd singular present of gam (gamāti = gacchati); part of the verse line vasa kuntini māgamāti.

nevayyakassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Rare word for 'grandfather', presumably a dialectal formation (cf. Sk. nāpitya?); doubtful. Genitive singular in the text. Occasionally written neyyaka.
nevayyakassa.example_2: 9. Nevayyakassa sīsañca [sīsaṃ vā (sī. syā. pī.)], hatthapādā ca dissare;
nevayyakassa.translation_2: But my grandsire’s head and feet are not to be seen;

abbhūḷhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In 1sg aorist (ending -iṃ, assimilated to -ī). Alternative forms in the text: abbūḷhaṃ and abbhūḷhaṃ, past participles meaning 'extracted'.
abbhūḷhaṃ.example_1: 11. Abbahī [abbūḷhaṃ (sī. syā.), abbhūḷhaṃ (ka.)] vata me sallaṃ, yamāsi hadayassitaṃ [sokaṃ hadayanissitaṃ (sī. syā.)];
abbhūḷhaṃ.translation_1: Indeed, you have extracted the dart that was lodged in my heart,

gattī.meaning_2: with limbs; having a body; whose limbs are
gattī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of candanalittagattā in the verse; a bahubbīhi adjective agreeing with sāmā. Nominative singular feminine.
gattī.example_1: 18. Sāmā ca [sāmāpi (sī. syā.)] kho candanalittagattā [gattī (ka. sī. syā. pī.)], laṭṭhīva sobhañjanakassa uggatā;
gattī.translation_1: And Ubbari, indeed, with limbs smeared in sandalwood, is as graceful as a shoot of the moringa tree risen up;

kisī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form kisī (kisā) agrees with assaṃ; variant reading in the text. Sometimes taken as kisa + ṇa.
kisī.example_1: 23. Sace rode kisā [kisī (pī.)] assaṃ, tassā me kiṃ phalaṃ siyā;
kisī.translation_1: If I were to weep, I would become emaciated; what fruit would that have for me?

vaṃka.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a monkey addressed by the Bodhisatta in the Jātaka verse; the reading is uncertain, perhaps a variant of vaṅka. Vocative singular in the text; treated here as an a-stem masculine.
vaṃka.example_1: Tasmā dhaṅka [vaṃka (pī.)] na socāmi, natthi soke dutīyatā [soko dutīyakā (ka.)].
vaṃka.translation_1: Therefore, Vanka, I do not sorrow; grief has no companionship.

kāraṇḍiya.meaning_2: Kāraṇḍiya (name of a person); O Karaṇḍiya
kāraṇḍiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative address in the text (variant koraṇḍiya in the printed text; Sinhalese and Burmese editions read kāraṇḍiya). Treated as a proper name; alternatively it may be a vocative of kāraṇḍava, so the gender is uncertain.
kāraṇḍiya.example_1: Punappunaṃ santaramānarūpo, koraṇḍiya [kāraṇḍiya (sī. syā. pī.)] ko nu tava yidhattho.
kāraṇḍiya.translation_1: Again and again, in a hurried manner, Koraṇḍiya, what is the purpose of this for you?

sānūni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative plural in the verse (sānūni ca pabbatāni ca). Not related to sānaṃ ('dog').
sānūni.example_2: Vikiriya sānūni ca pabbatāni ca, tasmā silaṃ dariyā pakkhipāmi.
sānūni.translation_2: Leveling the ridges and the mountains, therefore I throw the stone into the cave.

meko.meaning_2: by one; by a single person; one alone
meko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi resolution me + eko (by me + one); verse idiom, 'for one alone'. In the sentence: samaṃ manusso karaṇāya meko = 'for one man alone to make it level'.
meko.example_2: 36. Nayimaṃ mahiṃ arahati pāṇikappaṃ, samaṃ manusso karaṇāya meko;
meko.translation_2: 36. It is not possible for one human alone to make this earth level, as if by hand;

papothayeyyaṃ.meaning_2: would crush; would tread down; would trample
papothayeyyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 1st singular of papothayati (causative of pa + √puth). In the verse the speaker boasts he could crush even a hundred thousand such people with his left foot.
papothayeyyaṃ.example_2: Sataṃ sahassānipi tādisīnaṃ, vāmena pādena papothayeyyaṃ.
papothayeyyaṃ.translation_2: Even a hundred thousand of such as you, I could crush with my left foot.

ghosavā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular masculine of ghosavant, used of the sea. Alternative spelling ghosavā for ghosavā.
ghosavā.example_2: 55. Vāti gandho timirānaṃ, kusamuddo ca [va (syā. pī.)] ghosavā;
ghosavā.translation_2: The fragrance of the timira trees wafts, and the small sea is noisy;

sussondī.meaning_2: name of a woman; Suyonandī; Sussondī
sussondī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of suyonandī (CST reads suyonandī, other editions susandī or sussondī). Nominative singular in the verse.
sussondī.example_1: Dūre ito suyonandī [ito hi susandī (sī. syā.), itopi sussondī (pī.)], tambakāmā tudanti maṃ.
sussondī.translation_1: Sussondī is far from here, and desires for her, Tamba, torment my heart.

phalakenāhamaplaviṃ.meaning_2: on a plank I floated; by a plank I swam
phalakenāhamaplaviṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of phalakena (instrumental of phalaka, 'on a plank'), ahaṃ ('I') and aplaviṃ (aorist 1st singular of plavati, 'floated'). Perhaps also phalakena + ahaṃ + aplaviṃ with elision of final -a. Found in the verse about the ship broken by sea monsters.
phalakenāhamaplaviṃ.example_2: Makarehi abhidā [makarehibbhidā (sī.), makarehi ’ bhidā (syā.), makarehi bhinnā (pī.)] nāvā, phalakenāhamaplaviṃ.
phalakenāhamaplaviṃ.translation_2: The ship was broken by sea monsters, and I drifted on a plank.

uddharī.meaning_2: lifted up; raised; took up; carried
uddharī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of uddharati, used transitively with aṅgena (with the arm). The PEU entries give uddhara/uddhare as the underlying verb; the form uddharī is a common aorist variant (cf. akkharī-type endings).
uddharī.example_2: Aṅgena [aṅkena (pī. ka.)] uddharī bhaddā, mātā puttaṃva orasaṃ.
uddharī.translation_2: The lovely one lifted me with her arms, as a mother lifts her own son.

mandakkhī.meaning_2: with gentle eyes; of soft gaze
mandakkhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound meaning 'having gentle eyes', used as a feminine adjective in the verse (attanāpi ca mandakkhī). Stress is on the first syllable; the readings mandakkhī and mandākkhī occur.
mandakkhī.example_2: Attanāpi ca mandakkhī, evaṃ tamba vijānāhīti.
mandakkhī.translation_2: And with herself, the maiden of gentle gaze—thus, Tamba, understand it.

saṃvāsamabhirocaye.meaning_2: would not approve of living together (with); could not take delight in cohabitation (with)
saṃvāsamabhirocaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of saṃvāsaṃ (accusative of saṃvāsa, 'living together') + abhirocaye (optative 3rd singular of abhirocayati, 'approves of, finds pleasure in'). Found in the Jātaka verse Na dānāhaṃ tayā saddhiṃ, saṃvāsamabhirocaye. The idiom is saṃvāsaṃ (or saṃvāsāya) abhirocayati with the instrumental saddhiṃ = 'takes pleasure in living together with'.
saṃvāsamabhirocaye.translation_2: Then I do not desire to live together with you from now on.

setī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular present of seti (√si, to lie, sleep); the text reads setī by metrical lengthening. Used figuratively: 'in whom one rests like a son on a mother's breast'.
setī.example_2: Yasmiñca setī urasīva putto, sa ve mitto yo abhejjo parehīti.
setī.translation_2: But he in whom one rests like a son on a mother’s breast, he is indeed a friend who cannot be parted by others.

tavāhamasmī.meaning_2: I am yours; I am your servant
tavāhamasmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tava (your) + ahaṃ (I) + asmi (am). Part of the phrase tavāhamasmī ti. The final ī belongs to the quotation particle ti.
tavāhamasmī.example_2: 70. Hiriṃ tarantaṃ vijigucchamānaṃ, tavāhamasmī iti bhāsamānaṃ;
tavāhamasmī.translation_2: Who avoids shame, who loathes the state of being a friend, while saying, 'I am yours';

paccuvaso.meaning_2: hiding place; secret dwelling; lurking place
paccuvaso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading paccuvaso for maccuveso in the Jātaka verse; glosses the cave-dwelling of death ('that which stays over against/within'). Nominative singular in the text; compound analysis uncertain.
paccuvaso.translation_1: This is bait, a bond, and Death dwelling in the cave of the heart.

sāliya.meaning_2: young sāli bird; bird named Sāliya; (according to commentary) a head bull named Sāliya
sāliya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading sāḷiya; some editions read sāḷika. In this verse chāpoti is probably chāpo ti, so sāliya is nominative singular. The PEU entry understands sāliya as a bull's name, but the sentence context is a bird seizing a snake.
sāliya.example_1: 90. Yvāyaṃ sāḷiya [sāliya (sī. syā. pī.), sāḷika (?)] chāpoti, kaṇhasappaṃ agāhayi;
sāliya.translation_1: 90. As for the individual who made a young Sāḷiya bird seize a black snake;

āmanta.meaning_2: farewell; addressing; taking leave (of); "I bid you farewell"
āmanta.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in the fixed phrase āmanta kho taṃ gacchāma/gacchāmi, a parting formula. Probably a shortening of āmantayitvā or an absolutive of āmanteti ('having addressed, having taken leave'), used idiomatically as an indeclinable; the PEU entry analyses it as ā + manta + tvā. Kept as indeclinable, not as a verb form.

nayīdha.meaning_2: there is no here; not here
nayīdha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of na + idha, with -y- liaison; variant nayidha. Frequency in the verse suggests nacca-gīta is to be read as one dvandva ('dancing and singing'), not as two separate items.
nayīdha.example_2: Nayīdha naccagītaṃ vā [nayidha naccaṃ vā gītaṃ vā (sī. syā. pī.)], tāḷaṃ vā susamāhitaṃ;
nayīdha.translation_2: There is no dancing or singing here, nor any well-concentrated music,

dānī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An emphatic temporal particle, often following an imperative or future verb; in these verses it means 'now, at this moment'. Sometimes alternating with idāni.

sāḷiyamittavaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of sāḷiya (rice) + mitta (friend) + vara (best). Likely a proper name or epithet in the Jātaka verse. Nominative singular in the text.
sāḷiyamittavaro.example_2: Atha vaṇṇa sasīla hiri labhate, sumukhā visa sāḷiyamittavaro;
sāḷiyamittavaro.translation_2: Atha, Vaṇṇa, Sasīla, Hiri, Labhate, Sumukhā, Visa, Sāḷiya, Mittavara,

asamaṃvaguppari.meaning_2: unequalled and supreme; incomparable and highest
asamaṃvaguppari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A sandhi of asamaṃ (unequalled) and aguppari (supreme), occurring in a list of Jātaka names. The text asamaṃvaguppari has v for g; the commentary explains it as Asama and Vaggupari, but here it is taken as a single description.
asamaṃvaguppari.example_2: Jīnañca vaṇṇaṃ asamaṃvaguppari, sudesitā jātakanti santi vīsati [jātaka pañcavīsati (?)];
asamaṃvaguppari.translation_2: Jīna, Vaṇṇa, Asama, Vaggupari, these twenty-five Jātakas are well taught.

dummukkharūpā.meaning_2: of ugly speech; with bad utterance; misshapen in mouth
dummukkharūpā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Spelling varies between dummakkharūpā, dumukkharūpā and dummukkharūpā; nominative plural here, describing the mutterers of mantras.
dummukkharūpā.example_1: 10. Kharājinā jaṭilā paṅkadantā, dummakkharūpā [dumukkharūpā (sī. syā.), dummukkharūpā (pī. ka.)] yeme jappanti mante;
dummukkharūpā.translation_1: With goatskin garments, matted hair, and teeth stained with grime, those who mutter these sacred texts,

tassevāsā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of tassa cāsā; tassa + eva + āsā, with the eva-ā coalescence giving -evā-. Sometimes the second member is taken as āsā (hope) rather than the verb āsati.
tassevāsā.example_1: Tassa cāsā [tassevāsā (syā.)] samijjhati, tāva dūragatā satī;
tassevāsā.translation_1: His hope is fulfilled, though the mind is directed to what is far away;

sereyyakasseva.meaning_2: name of a plant (Barleria cristata?); the sereyyaka flower
sereyyakasseva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular with -ssa, joined with eva and written as one word (sereyyakassa eva). Name of a flower/plant; meaning uncertain.
sereyyakasseva.translation_2: Like a Sereyyaka flower, beautiful in color but without scent.

atuccaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular neuter, agreeing with an understood object of patasi in the Jātaka verse; the PEU analysis ati + ucca fits the sense 'too high'.
atuccaṃ.example_2: Atuccaṃ tāta patasi, abhūmiṃ tāta sevasi.
atuccaṃ.translation_2: You fly too high, dear one; you frequent a region that is not yours, dear one.

gijjhovātītasāsano.meaning_2: a vulture who has gone beyond the teaching; vulture disregarding the instruction
gijjhovātītasāsano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of gijjho (nom sg of gijjha, vulture) + atītasāsano (nom sg of atītasāsana, 'one whose instruction is past/transgressed'); an insulting epithet in the Jātaka verse. Sometimes written as a compound with the same meaning.
gijjhovātītasāsano.example_2: Atisīmacaro [atisīmaṃ caro (sī. syā. ka.)] ditto, gijjhovātītasāsano;
gijjhovātītasāsano.translation_2: Arrogant, wandering beyond the boundary, like a vulture who has passed by the teaching,

sārambhī.meaning_2: impetuous; irascible; prone to anger; quarrelsome
sārambhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of sārambha as an adjective of character in Jātaka verse (makkhī paḷāsī sārambhī); nom sg in the text.
sārambhī.example_2: 43. Makkhī paḷāsī sārambhī, issukī maccharī saṭho;
sārambhī.translation_2: The hypocrite, the wanton, the morose, / The man of envy, greed and treachery:

lohitape.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the verse (lohitape). Compound with pa from √pā 1 (drink); cf. lohitapāyī.
lohitape.translation_2: “Thou hast drunk my kindred’s blood, and robbed and slain them cruelly;

kukkuṭapothini.meaning_2: chicken-crusher; killer of chickens and cocks
kukkuṭapothini.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An abusive term for a woman (cori kukkuṭapothini). The text has -i for -ī; probably a compound of kukkuṭa and a feminine agent noun in -inī (cf. pothinī). Vocative or nominative singular in the verse.
kukkuṭapothini.translation_2: “Thou hast drunk my kindred’s blood, and robbed and slain them cruelly;

biḷārī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text, in the simile biḷārī viya kukkuṭaṃ (like a cat with a cock). The -ī marks the feminine of biḷāra.
biḷārī.example_2: Nenti saṇhāhi vācāhi, biḷārī viya kukkuṭaṃ.
biḷārī.translation_2: Lead him on with gentle words, like a cat with a cock.

biḷāriyāti.meaning_2: from the cat, it is said
biḷāriyāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of biḷāriyā (ablative singular of biḷārī, 'cat') with the quotative iti; the ending -ti in the text is the sandhi form. The cock is released 'from the cat'.
biḷāriyāti.translation_2: Is released from the enemy’s trap, like the cock from the cat.”

gāmanigamāsu.meaning_2: village and town; villages and towns
gāmanigamāsu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text (gāmanigamāsu), with -su doubled from sandhi with sādhu. A dvandva compound.
gāmanigamāsu.example_2: Dhammadhajo gāmanigamāsusādhu [gāmanigamāsu sādhusammato (sī.), gāmanigamasādhu (pī.)], dujjāno purisena bālisena.
gāmanigamāsu.translation_2: A 'Dhamma-banner' regarded as a saint in villages and towns, he is hard for a foolish man to discern.

bālisena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text: 'dujjāno purisena bālisena' — hard to be known by a foolish man. The PEU entry gives bālisa as 'ignorant, stupid, fool'.
bālisena.example_2: Dhammadhajo gāmanigamāsusādhu [gāmanigamāsu sādhusammato (sī.), gāmanigamasādhu (pī.)], dujjāno purisena bālisena.
bālisena.translation_2: A 'Dhamma-banner' regarded as a saint in villages and towns, he is hard for a foolish man to discern.

vipothatha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd plural in the text (vipothatha). The writer's variant vipothatha is glossed as viheṭhatha; from vi + √puth with the causative sign *e.
vipothatha.example_1: 69. Imaṃ tuṇḍehi pakkhehi, pādā cimaṃ viheṭhatha [vipothatha (pī.)];
vipothatha.translation_1: 69. Harass him with your beaks, with your wings, and with your feet;

añjhanaṃ.meaning_2: name of a grove; Añjana forest
añjhanaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. The edition reads añjhanaṃ; it is a proper name (Añjana forest) near Sāketa.
añjhanaṃ.example_1: 70. Sace brāhmaṇa gacchesi, sākete [sāketaṃ (sī. syā.)] ajjunaṃ [añjhanaṃ (sī. syā. pī.)] vanaṃ;
añjhanaṃ.translation_1: 70. If, brahmin, you go to the Añjana grove at Sāketa;

avabhottaṃ.meaning_2: eats unworthily; consumes improperly; eats without earning it
avabhottaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text avabhottaṃ is the infinitive avabhottuṃ (with variant reading avabhottaṃ), from √bhuj 1 with ava-; the present is not attested here. Meaning in the Atthakathā: to eat what one has not earned.
avabhottaṃ.example_1: Taṃ rājapiṇḍaṃ avabhottuṃ [avabhottaṃ (ka.)], nāhaṃ brāhmaṇa mussahe.
avabhottaṃ.translation_1: To consume that royal food unworthily, I shall not, brahmin.

ārajjuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in the verse as ārajjuṃ, accusative singular agreeing with dhanuṃ. The commentary glosses ārajjuṃ as ārajjaṃ, 'drawn, bent'. The PEU suggests a derivation ā + ranja + ṇya, but the formation is uncertain.
ārajjuṃ.example_1: Dhanuṃ ārajjaṃ [ārajjuṃ (niyya), adejjhaṃ (sī. pī.) advedhābhāvaṃ ekībhāvanti attho] katvāna, usuṃ sannayha [sandhāya (sī. pī.)] kosalo.
ārajjuṃ.translation_1: Having bent his bow and nocked an arrow.

apananda.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the Jātaka verse, listed among the ten kings. Singular in the text.
apananda.example_2: Apananda sirī ca sucittavaro, atha dhammika nandimigena dasāti.
apananda.translation_2: Apananda, Sirī, Sucittavaro, and then Dhammika and Nandimiga, are the ten.

bhayiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has bhayiyā, a variant spelling for the dative/genitive singular of bhariyā. The commentary's alternative bhayiyā na bhavissati suggests the variant reading bhariyāya is preferred.
bhayiyā.example_1: 80. Uttamatthaṃ labhitvāna, bhariyāya yo padassati [bhayiyā yo padassati (pī.), bhayiyā na bhavissati (ka.)];
bhayiyā.translation_1: 80. “Having obtained the highest benefit, one who gives it to his wife;

piyameti.meaning_2: regards as dear; thinks fondly of; holds dear
piyameti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has the variant li piyameti, glossed piyameti; the commentarial explanation takes piyaṃ + eti, 'goes to (what is) dear', i.e., holds dear. Compare the synonymous denominative piyāyati, from piya + *āya. The construction is uncertain.
piyameti.example_1: 81. Na ve piyammeti [na piyameti (ka.), na piyamedanti (katthaci)] janinda tādiso, attaṃ niraṃkatvā piyāni sevati [sevaye (?)];
piyameti.translation_1: 81. A person like you, O King, should not think, ‘This is my beloved,’ and having discarded oneself, pursue beloved things;

sevaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs as sevaye in the verse, an alternative or unmetrical reading (commentators give sevati); sevaye would be the optative 3rd singular 'should pursue; ought to pursue'. The main entry is the present stem sevati.
sevaye.example_1: 81. Na ve piyammeti [na piyameti (ka.), na piyamedanti (katthaci)] janinda tādiso, attaṃ niraṃkatvā piyāni sevati [sevaye (?)];
sevaye.translation_1: 81. A person like you, O King, should not think, ‘This is my beloved,’ and having discarded oneself, pursue beloved things;

paṭithaddhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular modifying sūciṃ ('needle') in the verse. The PEU entry suggests the word can also mean 'rough'.
paṭithaddhaṃ.translation_2: Strong enough to pierce an anvil, and very hard—who wishes to buy such a needle?

yañcatthaññaṃ.meaning_2: and whatever other; and whatever else
yañcatthaññaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yaṃ ca attha aññaṃ, an extended phrase meaning 'and whatever else there is'. Part of the stock phrase yañcatthaññaṃ ghare dhanaṃ, accusative/neut. In the text it is quoted speech.
yañcatthaññaṃ.example_2: Tayā ca maṃ nimanteyya, yañcatthaññaṃ ghare dhananti.
yañcatthaññaṃ.translation_2: He would invite me, and with you, he would offer whatever other wealth exists in the house.

tuṇḍila.meaning_2: name of a pig; Tuṇḍila; one who has a good snout
tuṇḍila.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the text, used to address the pig in the Jātaka verse. Peu derives it as tuṇḍa + ila, 'one who has a good mouth/snout'.
tuṇḍila.example_2: Appossukko bhuñja tuṇḍila, maṃsatthāya hi positāmhase [posiyāmase (sī. syā. pī.)].
tuṇḍila.translation_2: Eat, Tuṇḍila, contented; for we have been fattened for the sake of our flesh.

micche.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form micche in the verse is a metrical variant of micchā (or an Eastern ending); used adverbially with hiṃsituṃ, 'to harm wrongly'.
micche.example_2: 98. Mamañca disvāna pavaddhakāyaṃ, sabbo jano hiṃsitumeva micche;
micche.translation_2: Seeing that I have grown so great, all people would want to harm me;

disva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text written disva, a variant spelling of disvā (metrically shortened); the cpd disvāna is also found. Absolutive of √dis 'see' (present passati; dakkhati is the future/irregular present).
disva.example_1: Sāduñca thūlañca muduñca maṃsaṃ, kākāpi maṃ disvāna [disva (sī. pī.)] viheṭhayeyyuṃ.
disva.translation_1: My meat is sweet, thick, and soft; even crows, upon seeing me, would torment me.
disva.example_2: 41. Etādisaṃ brāhmaṇa disvāna [disva (sī. pī.)] yakkhaṃ, puccheyya poso sukhamāsisāno [sukhamāsasāno (syā.), sukhamāsisamāno (ka.)];
disva.translation_2: “Having seen such a spirit, O brahmin, a wise person should ask, hoping for their own welfare;

dāyadā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural in the verse (dāyadā). Sometimes analysed as dāyāda; cf. dāya + √dā.
dāyadā.example_1: Rājāno atha vā corā, dāyadā ye va [ye ca (syā. ka.)] appiyā;
dāyadā.translation_1: Kings, or robbers, or heirs who are not dear to him;

sakkohamasmī.meaning_2: I am Sakka; Sakka am I
sakkohamasmī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sakko ahaṃ asmi, the speaker naming himself as Sakka, lord of the thirty gods (tidasānaminda). Appears at the end of a verse line in the Jātaka.
sakkohamasmī.example_2: Ahañca te nāmadheyyaṃ vadāmi, sakkohamasmī tidasānamindo.
sakkohamasmī.translation_2: As for myself, my title I proclaim, / Sakka, the lord whom thirty gods obey.

ajjaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text ajjaṃ is ajja with an added ṃ, probably for the metre (v. 1 ajjaṃ hārayiṃ). It is an indeclinable, so the ending is not a real case ending. Some editions read ajja instead.
ajjaṃ.example_1: Cirassaṃ nhāpitaṃ laddhā, lomaṃ taṃ ajjaṃ hārayiṃ [apahārayiṃ (sī. pī.)].
ajjaṃ.translation_1: Having finally found a barber, I have had that hair removed today.”

apahārayiṃ.meaning_2: has removed; has had removed; takes away
apahārayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular in -iṃ (with variant reading apahārayiṃ); here 'I had (the hair) removed', i.e. had it cut off. Causative of apaharati (apa + √har).
apahārayiṃ.example_1: Cirassaṃ nhāpitaṃ laddhā, lomaṃ taṃ ajjaṃ hārayiṃ [apahārayiṃ (sī. pī.)].
apahārayiṃ.translation_1: Having finally found a barber, I have had that hair removed today.”

massuyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text massuyā is instrumental singular. sukatāya massuyā means 'with a well-trimmed beard'.
massuyā.example_2: 139. Tvaññeva maṇinā channo, sukatāya ca massuyā;
massuyā.translation_2: “You are indeed suited by that gem and by that well-trimmed beard;

tuṇḍilako.meaning_2: name of a bird (Tuṇḍila); one with a prominent beak
tuṇḍilako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the verse; listed among the birds and animals of the Jātaka. PEU derives it from tuṇḍa + ila, 'having a beak/mouth'.
tuṇḍilako.example_2: Atha passa sasūci ca tuṇḍilako, miga mayhakapañcamapakkhivaro;
tuṇḍilako.translation_2: The Needle, the Tuṇḍila, the Deer, the Mayhaka, the fifth is the Best of Birds,

mayhakapañcamapakkhivaro.meaning_2: the Mayhaka (bird) and the fifth, the best of birds
mayhakapañcamapakkhivaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name in a list of birds in the Jātaka verse (miga mayhaka pañcama pakkhivara). Nominative singular in the text.
mayhakapañcamapakkhivaro.example_2: Atha passa sasūci ca tuṇḍilako, miga mayhakapañcamapakkhivaro;
mayhakapañcamapakkhivaro.translation_2: The Needle, the Tuṇḍila, the Deer, the Mayhaka, the fifth is the Best of Birds,

saravaraveganiddhutaṃ.meaning_2: struck down by the speed of the excellent arrow; pierced by the swift speed of the arrow
saravaraveganiddhutaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound with niddhuta (pp of niddhunāti). Accusative singular modifying migādhipaṃ in the verse.
saravaraveganiddhutaṃ.translation_2: Look at the highest one who associates with the low, the king of beasts, struck down by the speed of the excellent arrow.

mupanamaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (sī. pī. a. ni.) in place of seṭṭhamupagamaṃ; resolved as sandhi of mu + upanamaṃ, where upanamaṃ is a present participle of upanamati. Accusative in the sentence.
mupanamaṃ.example_1: Seṭṭhamupagamaṃ [mupanamaṃ (sī. pī. a. ni.3.26)] udeti khippaṃ, tasmāttanā uttaritaraṃ [tasmā attano uttariṃ (sī. pī.), tasmā attano uttaraṃ (syā.)] bhajethāti.
mupanamaṃ.translation_1: Approaching the highest, one rises quickly; therefore, associate with those superior to yourself.

sūpitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a past participle used adjectivally with bhikkhaṃ, 'food seasoned with curry'. Related to sūpa, 'curry'. The PEU entry connects it with sūpasampanna.
sūpitaṃ.translation_2: 16. Come inside, young man, with your seasoned food,

āyuro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name. Nominative singular āyuro in the text. Not from āyus (life).
āyuro.example_2: 41. Byākāsi āyuro pañhaṃ, atthaṃ [attha (pī. sī. niyya)] dhammassa kovido;
āyuro.translation_2: Ayura has solved my question, wise in all philosophy;

dijivhaṃ.meaning_2: two-tongued; having a double tongue; snake; serpent
dijivhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet of a serpent. Accusative singular in the text; the Siamese and PTS editions read dujivhaṃ.
dijivhaṃ.example_1: 49. Ādāya daṇḍaṃ parisumbha bhastaṃ, passeḷamūgaṃ uragaṃ dujivhaṃ [dijivhaṃ (sī. pī.)];
dijivhaṃ.translation_1: Taking a stick, beat the bag; look at the serpent with the double tongue, drooling at the mouth.

aṭṭhisena.meaning_2: Atthisena; name of a Brahmin (in the Jātaka verse)
aṭṭhisena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name, probably aṭṭhi + sena (having an army of bones?); some editions read atthisena. Declined as an a-stem; in the text it is used in the vocative.
aṭṭhisena.example_2: 54. Yeme ahaṃ na jānāmi, aṭṭhisena vanibbake;
aṭṭhisena.translation_2: 54. Atthisena, I do not know those beggars;

pasāsanāto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Ablative singular in the text (pasāsanāto, with variant pasāsanito). Used with nikkhanto: 'having emerged from ruling'. The PEU entries pasāsanta and pasāsana take √sās with the -anta and -ana suffixes; the commentary may prefer pasāsati here. If analysed as an adjective, pos would be adj.
pasāsanāto.example_1: Pasāsanato [pasāsanito (sī. syā.), pasāsanāto (pī.)] nikkhanto, idha dāni pasāsasi.
pasāsanāto.translation_1: Having emerged from ruling, why do you now rule here?

atthasandassanī.meaning_2: showing the meaning; demonstrating the benefit; revealing the truth
atthasandassanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Jātaka Aṭṭhakathā, added to explain sandassanī as 'shedding light on the meaning'. Nominative singular feminine, agreeing with katā; the meaning of sandassanī here is doubtful ('instructive' or 'pointing to the meaning').
atthasandassanī.example_2: 89. Esā te upamā rāja, taṃ suṇohi arindama [atthasandassanī katā (pī.)];
atthasandassanī.translation_2: 89. This is a simile for you, O king, listen to it, subduer of enemies;

karaṇḍunāma.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the name Karaṇḍu with nāma ('named'), variant reading for karaṇḍako in the text; the name itself refers to the Kalinga king.
karaṇḍunāma.translation_1: 94. Karaṇḍaka of the Kalingas, and Naggaji of the Gandharas;

bhaggavi.meaning_2: Bhaggavī (name of a woman; feminine of Bhaggava)
bhaggavi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative singular in the verse, addressed to a woman named Bhaggavī. The PEU notes bhaggavī as the feminine of bhaggava (a potter's name).
bhaggavi.example_2: Ahampi eko carissāmi bhaggavi, hitvāna kāmāni yathodhikāni.
bhaggavi.translation_2: I too, Bhaggavi, will wander alone, having abandoned sensual pleasures as they are.

aparāyiṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading aparāyaṇī. Nominative singular describing a woman. Compound of na + parāyaṇa; the text's apparatus notes the alternative spelling.
aparāyiṇī.example_1: 100. Sā nūnāhaṃ marissāmi, abandhu aparāyinī [aparāyiṇī (sī.), aparāyaṇī (?)];
aparāyiṇī.translation_1: 100. Surely I shall die, kinless and unprotected,

aparāyaṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has the variant aparāyinī; the form here is aparāyaṇī, feminine nominative singular agreeing with the speaker. Built with the negative prefix na (a-).
aparāyaṇī.example_1: 100. Sā nūnāhaṃ marissāmi, abandhu aparāyinī [aparāyiṇī (sī.), aparāyaṇī (?)];
aparāyaṇī.translation_1: 100. Surely I shall die, kinless and unprotected,

pavīṇati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person singular present of pavīṇati, occurring in the Jātaka verse Yāvatāsīsatī poso tāvadeva pavīṇati. It appears to mean 'honours, respects', though the form is rare and possibly uncertain; the PEU entry gives the same analysis.
pavīṇati.translation_2: 101. A person frequents another only as long as they have hopes,

oṭṭhibyādhiṃva.meaning_2: like a camel disease; as if a camel's sickness
oṭṭhibyādhiṃva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] oṭṭhibyādhi (camel disease) + iva; some analyses take oṭṭhi as 'camel' and byādhi as 'sickness'. Accusative singular in the verse, used in a simile about a khattiya being abandoned.
oṭṭhibyādhiṃva.translation_2: When those benefits fail, they abandon him, like an aristocrat abandoning a sick camel.

manubujjhati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Commentarial/verse sandhi of maṃ + ujjhati (understands me). 3rd singular in the text; the dictionary reading is often manubujjhati for maṃ anubujjhati. Uncertain analysis.
manubujjhati.translation_2: 103. Whoever is one to whom a kindness has been done before, and has had his needs fulfilled, and realizes it,

chijjito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading; other editions have vacchito, vicchito. Past participle used adjectivally in the simile of a tender shoot cut off. The passive stem chijja comes from √chid with the -ya sign and assimilation of d.
chijjito.example_1: 106. Ayaṃ vā so mato seti, allasiṅgaṃva vacchito [allapiṅkava chijjito (sī. pī.), allapītaṃva vicchito (syā.)];
chijjito.translation_1: Either he lies here dead, like a tender shoot cut off,

bhumyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular; bhumyā is the sandhi form with the locative ending -yā. In the text it means 'on the ground'.

rajjuvālambanī.meaning_2: depending on a rope; hanging from a rope
rajjuvālambanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Simile for household delight: it hangs by a rope. Nominative singular feminine agreeing with rati. Sometimes taken as a compound noun in -ī; the second member is from ālambana (support, hanging on).
rajjuvālambanī.example_2: 120. Rajjuvālambanī cesā, yā gehe vasato rati;
rajjuvālambanī.translation_2: This delight in home is like a hanging rope;

byādhase.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Text variant byādhase (2sg); alternative readings byadhase, byādhasi. Root √vyath with vy > by and loss of th; compare byādha 'hunter'.
byādhase.example_1: Dhārayaṃ byathasi [byādhase (sī.), byadhase (pī.), byādhasi (ka.)] bhītā [bhīto (sī. syā. pī.)], kamatthaṃ koṭasimbali [koṭisimbali (sī. pī.)].
byādhase.translation_1: You shake with fear while bearing it; for what reason, O Koṭasimbali?

byadhase.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Second person singular byadhase (also read byādhase, byādhasi) in the verse. The variant readings suggest √vyath with a passive-looking -se ending, but the sense is active: 'you tremble'.
byadhase.example_1: Dhārayaṃ byathasi [byādhase (sī.), byadhase (pī.), byādhasi (ka.)] bhītā [bhīto (sī. syā. pī.)], kamatthaṃ koṭasimbali [koṭisimbali (sī. pī.)].
byadhase.translation_1: You shake with fear while bearing it; for what reason, O Koṭasimbali?

nivātajā.meaning_2: growing in a sheltered place; grown in a windless spot; sheltered (of plants)
nivātajā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse nivātajā agrees with rukkhā in mama passe nivātajā, 'the trees growing in my sheltered place'. Sometimes analysed as nivāta + jana + kvi, but here ja (from √jan 'be born, grow') fits the metre and meaning.
nivātajā.example_2: 124. Te rukkhā saṃvirūhanti, mama passe nivātajā;
nivātajā.translation_2: Those trees will sprout from seeds protected from the wind upon my branches;

nisādetvā.meaning_2: having seated; having placed (on); having made sit
nisādetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of nisīdati (caus. nisādeti); variant spelling of nisīdetvā in the second verse. Used with ucchaṅge: 'having seated (me) on the lap'.
nisādetvā.translation_2: Having made my mind clear toward them, having seated them on a spread of leaves;

sākhamakampayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative aorist 3rd singular in -i (akampayi), contracted from akampayī; the text reads sākhaṃ akampayi. The verse refers to one who made a bough shake. Causative meaning is clear from the context.
sākhamakampayi.example_2: Akkhātaṃ nūna taṃ tena, yo taṃ sākhamakampayi.
sākhamakampayi.translation_2: Surely that has been declared to you by the one who shook that bough.

avajjhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for avañci at Ja 160; aorist 2nd singular. The commentary takes it from √vadh 'to kill'. The PEU entry avajjha 'not to be killed' suggests some confusion with the negative compound; here it is a verb form.
avajjhi.example_1: 160. Tatheva tvaṃ avedesi, avañci [avajjhi (ka.)] pitaraṃ mama;
avajjhi.translation_1: 160. So too you have known, you have killed my father;

kumbhimapassayitvā.meaning_2: having set the pot (on the hearth); having put the pot
kumbhimapassayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kumbhiṃ (accusative of kumbhī 'pot') and apassayitvā, absolutive of apassayati 'to set (on a hearth)'; the reading kumbhimadhissayitvā in the text is a variant.
kumbhimapassayitvā.example_1: 1. Odātavatthā suci allakesā, kaccāni kiṃ kumbhimadhissayitvā [kumbhimapassayitvā (pī.)];
kumbhimapassayitvā.translation_1: 1. Robed in white, with dripping hair, Kaccānī, why have you set the pot upon the hearth?

taveta.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular of the pronoun tvaṃ. Here in the sandhi form taveva (tava + eva), meaning “has told you”. Variant reading taveta.
taveta.example_1: 3. Anuvicca kaccāni karohi kiccaṃ, dhammo mato ko nu taveva [taveta (sī. syā. pī.)] saṃsi;
taveta.translation_1: 3. Having closely examined, Kaccānī, perform your duty; who has told you that Right is dead?

miyyatī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Irregular passive form of √mar (marati), with -yy- for -r-. In the text it is miyyatī, with the final -ī caused by sandhi before the following word; the meaning here is 'dies, perishes'. Conjectured variant of miyyati.
miyyatī.example_2: Sahassanetto atulānubhāvo, na miyyatī dhammavaro kadāci.
miyyatī.translation_2: The thousand-eyed one of incomparable power—the noble Dhamma never dies.

ghuṇo.meaning_2: weevil; wood-worm; insect that bores into wood
ghuṇo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the verse (ghuṇo). The PEU entry splits it as ghuṇa + a; the sense is a weevil that does not relish hard wood (sāre).
ghuṇo.example_2: Khīṇabhakkho mahārāja, sāre na ramatī ghuṇo.
ghuṇo.translation_2: Hard wood a weevil liketh not, though other food runs low.

lahumatthavicintikā.meaning_2: quick to consider what is beneficial; one who swiftly thinks out the meaning
lahumatthavicintikā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading lahumatthavicintikā, compound of lahu + attha + vicintika. Feminine nominative singular in the verse, agreeing with itthī.
lahumatthavicintikā.example_1: Itthīpi paṇḍitā hoti, lahuṃ atthaṃ vicintikā [lahumatthavicintikā (sī. pī.)].
lahumatthavicintikā.translation_1: A woman also is learned, one who quickly thinks out what is worthwhile.

avekkhiya.meaning_2: having looked at; having examined; having considered
avekkhiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive of avekkhati, used in the text twice with the sense 'having considered for oneself'; the form avekkhiya is an -iya absolutive.

upāyaso.meaning_2: with skill; wisely; with sagacity; by means of wisdom
upāyaso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in the Jātaka verse dhammena ñāyena upāyaso nayaṃ. The ending -so is probably an adverbial suffix (cf. -to/-so), giving the sense 'by way of wisdom, wisely'; the PEU entries upāyana/upāyati are not related in meaning.
upāyaso.example_2: 35. Evaṃ sunītena [suvinītena (pī.)] subhāsitena, dhammena ñāyena upāyaso nayaṃ;
upāyaso.translation_2: Thus, with well-spoken words, with the qualities, with wisdom, and with skillful means, guiding the way,

patva.meaning_2: having reached; having attained; having come (to)
patva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text patva stands for patvā, the absolutive of pāpuṇāti (√ap with the prefix pa), the -tvā dropped before the next word. Some editions read patvā.
patva.example_2: Pāvekkhi pathaviṃ cecco, hīnatto patva pariyāyaṃ [attapariyāyaṃ (sī. syā.), pattapariyāyaṃ (ka. sī. niyya)].
patva.translation_2: The King Cetiya, reduced to a base state, entered the earth when his time had come.

māmiva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of maṃ (accusative of amha, 'me') + iva ('like, as'). In the verse pappoti māmiva means 'reaches me, as it were / like me'. Sometimes analysed as mā + iva or mama + iva.
māmiva.translation_2: King Sivi, I have fallen into the hands of foes like one who has lost everything;

kumudinī.meaning_2: abounding in white water-lilies; full of kumuda lotuses; a lake covered with lotuses
kumudinī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these verses it is an adjective describing the Gaṅgā and the Kokilā rivers, "full of white lotuses". The PEU analysis takes it as kumuda + ṇa + inī; the ṇa suffix is not evident in the form and the analysis is uncertain.
kumudinī.example_2: 77. Gaṅgā kumudinī santā, saṅkhavaṇṇā ca kokilā;
kumudinī.translation_2: When the Ganges is calm like a lotus-tank, and cuckoos are pearl-white,

gaṇacāriṇī.meaning_2: moving in a troop; travelling in a swarm
gaṇacāriṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes makkhikā (flies) in the verse; nominative singular in the text.
gaṇacāriṇī.translation_2: When swarms of flies, having drunk their fill of strong drink,

pulasa.meaning_2: kind of lotus or water plant (its leaves used for umbrellas); (variant reading for muḷāla)
pulasa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in the compound muḷāla-pulasa at Jātaka 85, with variant readings pulāsa and muḷāla alone. The word is rare and its exact botanical referent is uncertain; probably a water plant whose leaves make umbrellas.
pulasa.example_1: 85. Yadā muḷāla [pulasa (sī. pī.), pulāsa (syā.)] pattānaṃ, chattaṃ thirataraṃ siyā;
pulasa.translation_1: When an umbrella made of lotus-leaves is firmer,

pulāsa.meaning_2: lotus leaf; lotus petal; covering made of lotus leaves
pulāsa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of muḷāla / pulasa in the verse; part of a compound with pattānaṃ in the sentence.
pulāsa.example_1: 85. Yadā muḷāla [pulasa (sī. pī.), pulāsa (syā.)] pattānaṃ, chattaṃ thirataraṃ siyā;
pulāsa.translation_1: When an umbrella made of lotus-leaves is firmer,

kuluṅko.meaning_2: name of a bird; a small bird
kuluṅko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading kulako in the text; nominative singular. The PEU suggestions kulumba/kulumpa are unrelated.
kuluṅko.example_1: 86. Yadā kulako [kuluṅko (sī. pī.), kuluko (syā.)] sakuṇo, pabbataṃ gandhamādanaṃ;
kuluṅko.translation_1: When a tiny bird, the kulako,

pothayitvāna.meaning_2: having beaten; having struck; having hit
pothayitvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for heṭhayitvāna in the verse; absolute form of pothayati (< √puth, caus).
pothayitvāna.example_1: 89. Naṅguṭṭhaṃ me avakkamma [apakkamma (ka.)], heṭhayitvāna [pothayitvāna (ka.)] eḷike [eḷaki (syā.), eḷiki (pī.)];
pothayitvāna.translation_1: “You have trodden upon my tail, goat, and injured me;

eḷiki.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of eḷakī, vocative singular addressing a she-goat in Jātaka verse 89. Some editions read eḷaki or eḷike.
eḷiki.example_1: 89. Naṅguṭṭhaṃ me avakkamma [apakkamma (ka.)], heṭhayitvāna [pothayitvāna (ka.)] eḷike [eḷaki (syā.), eḷiki (pī.)];
eḷiki.translation_1: “You have trodden upon my tail, goat, and injured me;

sabbhiṃ.meaning_2: with the virtuous; by the good; with good men
sabbhiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrantive plural of santa ("virtuous, good"), used adverbially with the sense "with the good". Sometimes written saddhiṃ after sandhi; here sabbhiṃ. Not related to saddhiṃ ("together with"). Instrumental plural in the text.
sabbhiṃ.example_2: Nikkamaṃ duṭṭhe yuñjetha, so ca sabbhiṃ na rañjatīti.
sabbhiṃ.translation_2: One should apply effort against the wicked, for he does not delight in the virtuous.”

bahudhaso.meaning_2: in many ways; in abundance; plentifully
bahudhaso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text; the editions differ (bahuttaso, pahuttato, pahūtaso). Likely an adverb from bahu with the distributive suffix -dhaso. Meaning in the sentence is uncertain.
bahudhaso.example_1: Tesaṃ ajagaramedaṃ, accahāsi bahuttaso [pahuttato (ka. sī.), pahūtaso (syā. pī.), bahudhaso (ka.)].
bahudhaso.translation_1: He brought them much [food] from the snake-mountain.

māmari.meaning_2: name of a bird (red-breasted?); a species of bird addressed as a vocative
māmari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative in lohitatuṇḍa māmari; the second word may be a bird's name, or an exclamation. Meaning uncertain; the related entry māmaka is not connected.
māmari.example_2: 21. Cara cārikaṃ lohitatuṇḍa māmari, kiṃ tvaṃ suva sukkhadumamhi jhāyasi;
māmari.translation_2: Go on your journey (cārikaṃ), Redbeak, do not linger; why, parrot, do you pine upon a withered tree?

sākhavā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of sākhāvant (sākhā + vant). In the first text it may agree with a masculine noun (nominative singular -vā); in the second it appears in the nominative, perhaps as the subject, with the tree (the 'branchy one') standing. Compare sākhāvant.
sākhavā.example_2: So sākhavā phalimā saṃvirūḷho, madhutthiko tiṭṭhatu sobhamāno.
sākhavā.translation_2: May it stand, rich in branches and fruit, grown luxuriantly and full of honey-sweetness, shining.

upabhuñjimhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person plural aorist; the PEU entry gives 'they enjoyed' but -imhā is 1st plural ('we enjoyed'), which fits the verse. The form is upabhuñjimhā, not upabhuñjimha.
upabhuñjimhā.translation_2: Long years we have enjoyed the luscious fruit it bare,

opattamaphalaṃ.meaning_2: with fallen leaves and fruit; whose leaves and fruit have dropped
opattamaphalaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of opatta (fallen off, pp of opatati) + phala. Accusative singular qualifying dumaṃ: 'a tree whose leaves and fruit have fallen'. The text's opattam- shows sandhi of opattaṃ + phalaṃ as separate words (opattaṃ aphalaṃ?) is possible; construed here as a compound.
opattamaphalaṃ.translation_2: Nor leaves nor fruit it yields, alas! the tree is dead;

gītakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text; a variant reading for gāthakaṃ. Diminutive of gīta, from √gā (sing).
gītakaṃ.example_1: Vuyhamānaka bhaddante, ekaṃ me dehi gāthakaṃ [gītakaṃ (ka. aṭṭha.)].
gītakaṃ.translation_1: Good sir, as I am being swept away, give me just one song.

nipīḷeti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative form with active ending -ti; occurs in verse as nipīḷeti. The prefix ni- gives the sense of pressing down or crushing. Present 3rd singular.
nipīḷeti.example_2: Sā me sīsaṃ nipīḷeti, jātaṃ saraṇato bhayaṃ.
nipīḷeti.translation_2: That crushes my head; fear has arisen from my refuge.

loṇiyateliyāni.meaning_2: salted and oiled; with salt and oil; sprinkled with salt and oil
loṇiyateliyāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of loṇiya (salted) + teliya (oiled). In the text it is nominative plural neuter agreeing with annāni. The PEU analysis loṇiya + teliya is followed; alternative loṇa + iya and tela + iya analyses are possible.
loṇiyateliyāni.example_2: 74. Ahampi maṃsāni phalāni bhuñje, annāni ca loṇiyateliyāni;
loṇiyateliyāni.translation_2: I too eat meat and fruits, and rice with salt and oil;

tussasī.meaning_2: is satisfied (with); is pleased (with); is content (with)
tussasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular present of tussati, in the idiom na tussasī ("you are not satisfied"); the ending -si is used in verse.
tussasī.example_2: Na tussasī rukkhaphalehi dhaṅka, maṃsāni vā yāni susānamajjhe.
tussasī.translation_2: You are not satisfied with tree fruits, crow, or with the meat that is in the middle of the cemetery.

accupasevato.meaning_2: very devoted (to); constantly associating (with); excessively following
accupasevato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound in the genitive singular: 'of one who is very devoted to'. From ati + upasevanta, with sandhi ti + u > ccu.
accupasevato.translation_2: 85. Evils increase, dear one, for one who constantly follows the fool;

saṃgañchi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of saṃgacchati in the text; 2nd person singular present. The form is a ṃa-infixed present of √gam, but the class is irregular; it is used with the instrumental (bālena).
saṃgañchi.example_1: Māssu bālena saṃgacchi [saṃgañchi (sī. pī.)], dukkho bālehi saṅgamoti.
saṃgañchi.translation_1: do not associate with a fool; association with fools is suffering.

aññamabhippamodayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of aññaṃ (accusative of añña, 'another') and abhippamodayi, aorist 3rd singular of abhippamodayati ('delights; gladdens'). The reading may also be taken as aññaṃ + abhippamodayi with the sandhi -ṃ > -m before a vowel.
aññamabhippamodayi.example_2: Yathā have pāṇarivettha rakkhitā, duṭṭhā mayī aññamabhippamodayi.
aññamabhippamodayi.translation_2: As if guarded here, the wicked one delighted with another, even while I was watching.

jotirivā.meaning_2: like a flame; like a fire; like a light
jotirivā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of joti + iva (flame + like). In the texts the form is divided as jotirivā, with a sandhi r, and iva is lengthened to ivā at the verse end. Instrumental-like comparison: 'like a flame in the forest by an ascetic'.
jotirivā.example_2: 92. Divā ca ratto ca mayā upaṭṭhitā, tapassinā jotirivā vane vasaṃ;
jotirivā.translation_2: She was established by me during the day and during the night, as a flame is in the forest by an ascetic.

pajjhāti.meaning_2: broods (over); pines (for); is dejected and sorrowful
pajjhāti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Only the 3rd singular is attested; the verse has aorist pajjhāyi (see separate entry). Sinhalese editions also read pajjhāyati.
pajjhāti.example_1: Pajjhāyi [pajjhāti (sī. pī.), pajjhāyati (sī. niyya)] paṭigacchantiṃ, āgataṃ meṇḍa [meḷa (sī. pī.)] mātaraṃ.
pajjhāti.translation_1: She broods over the she-goat who has returned, having come [to her].”
pajjhāti.example_2: Pūtimaṃsova pajjhāyi [pajjhāti (sī. pī.), pajjhāyati (sī. niyya)], yo akāle vipekkhati.
pajjhāti.translation_2: He who stares at the wrong time broods like Putimansa.”

paṭigacchantiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine accusative singular agreeing with mātaraṃ in the verse; the calf is said to return to its mother. Some editions read paṭigacchanti.
paṭigacchantiṃ.example_2: Pajjhāyi [pajjhāti (sī. pī.), pajjhāyati (sī. niyya)] paṭigacchantiṃ, āgataṃ meṇḍa [meḷa (sī. pī.)] mātaraṃ.
paṭigacchantiṃ.translation_2: She broods over the she-goat who has returned, having come [to her].”

meḷa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading meḷa for meṇḍa (goat; ram). The text form is accusative singular; the spelling with ḷ is found in the Sinhalese and PTS editions.
meḷa.example_1: Pajjhāyi [pajjhāti (sī. pī.), pajjhāyati (sī. niyya)] paṭigacchantiṃ, āgataṃ meṇḍa [meḷa (sī. pī.)] mātaraṃ.
meḷa.translation_1: She broods over the she-goat who has returned, having come [to her].”

sañjīvito.meaning_2: revived; brought back to life; restored
sañjīvito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used predicatively in the verse: pati sañjīvito mayhaṃ, 'my husband has been revived'. Alternative analysis: name of a hell, but not applicable here.
sañjīvito.example_2: Pati sañjīvito mayhaṃ, eyyāsi piyapucchikā [pucchitā (syā. ka.)].
sañjīvito.translation_2: My husband has been brought back to life; come, you who ask after my loved one.”

āḷino.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The form is dative/genitive singular of āḷi; here it qualifies vaccha (friend), so the sense 'friend; companion' fits the context.
āḷino.example_2: Ārogyaṃ āḷino vajjaṃ [vacchaṃ (?)], idheva vasa māgamāti.
āḷino.translation_2: The danger for a friend is health; stay right here in this life, do not come.”

nipātaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular would be nipātaye; here the form may also be read as optative in the verse ('where he might strike'). Could also be caus of nipatati. See also nipātayoga.
nipātaye.example_2: Padesaṃ taṃ na passāmi, yattha dāṭhaṃ nipātaye.
nipātaye.translation_2: I see no place on him where I might strike my fangs.

kānissa.meaning_2: what are for him; what are his
kānissa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of kāni (neuter plural of ka) + assa (genitive singular of ima). In the text it introduces the questions about the man's life-paths; commentarial gloss may vary.
kānissa.translation_2: What are the life-paths of this man, by which his way of life is known?

kuliṅkā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternate reading for kulīkā in the verse; nominative singular used as the subject of the passive participle baddhā. The PEU entry gives kuliṅga as 'sparrow'.
kuliṅkā.example_1: 112. Baddhā kulīkā [kuliṅkā (sī. pī.)] mitamāḷhakena, akkhā jitā [akkhācitā (sī. aṭṭha.)] saṃyamo abbhatīto;
kuliṅkā.translation_1: He has bound birds with a measure of grain, he has abandoned his restraint;

oruddhapaṭiruddhosmi.meaning_2: I am obstructed and blocked; I am hemmed in and trapped
oruddhapaṭiruddhosmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of a compound (oruddha + paṭiruddha) with the verb amhi, assimilated to -osmi in verse. Both participles are pp of rundhati/rundhati with prefix o-/paṭi-. Subject is first person singular.
oruddhapaṭiruddhosmi.translation_2: I am hemmed in and trapped; what evil have I fashioned?

māviddhaṃ.meaning_2: let it not be pierced; may it not be fixed (on); not pierced
māviddhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mā (prohibitive particle) + āviddhaṃ (pp of āvijjhati, 'pierced; fixed'), the final -ā of mā elided before ā-. Agrees with cakkaṃ (nt, nominative singular); mā with the aorist pamokkhasīti punningly, the wheel is 'not to be loosed'.
māviddhaṃ.example_2: Cakkaṃ te sirasi [sirasmi (syā.)] māviddhaṃ, na taṃ jīvaṃ pamokkhasīti.
māviddhaṃ.translation_2: The circlet is fixed upon your head; you shall not be released from it while alive.

āsaṅgī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the Jātaka verse āsaṅgī bahupāyāso describes anger as clinging and bringing much distress. Nom sg in the text; printed with a capital in the second occurrence.
āsaṅgī.example_2: Āsaṅgī bahupāyāso, tasmā kodhaṃ na rocaye.
āsaṅgī.translation_2: it is clinging and causes much distress; therefore, I do not desire anger.”

maṃkate.meaning_2: done by me; caused by me; on account of me
maṃkate.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of the pronoun maṃ (me) and kata (done). The text writes maṃ-kate with a hyphen; the locative singular agrees with kassaci. The commentary explains it as "due to me".
maṃkate.example_2: Na mano vā sarīraṃ vā, maṃ-kate sakka kassaci;
maṃkate.translation_2: may no creature, because of me, ever be harmed in body or in mind,

subhmā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading subhmā (for subbhā/subhū) in the verse; here likely nominative singular of subha used adjectivally of a person, 'beautiful'. Some editions read subbhū or subhā.
subhmā.example_1: 40. Subbhū [subbhā (syā.), sumbhā, subhmā (ka.)] subhā suppaṭimukkakambu, paggayha sovaṇṇamayāya pātiyā;
subhmā.translation_1: “With a beautiful face, beautiful, wearing fine golden ornaments, lifting up a golden plate,

subbhu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of subbhū, used in the Jātaka verse as a vocative addressing a woman. The related PEU entry takes the second member from bhū (eyebrow).
subbhu.example_1: Susoṇi subbhamu [subbhu (sī.), subbhā (syā.)] suvilaggamajjhe [suvilākamajjhe (syā. pī. sī. aṭṭha.), suvilātamajjhe (ka.)], kissa me kammassa ayaṃ vipāko.
subbhu.translation_1: O lovely-browed, beautiful-browed, slender-waisted one, what kamma of mine has resulted in this?”

paṭipādayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative paṭipādayati (√pad, 'go', caus. 'cause to go, procure, provide'). In the verse it means 'procured, provided' the conch-shell shoes. PEU's glosses ('compared, accepted, believed') do not fit; 'presented, gave' is the contextual sense. The -ī ending is 3rd singular aorist.
paṭipādayī.example_2: Paṭipādayī saṅkha upāhanāni [upāhanāhi (sī. pī.)], sā dakkhiṇā kāmaduhā tavajja.
paṭipādayī.translation_2: who had blistered feet, was thirsty, and weary; that gift is your Cow of Plenty today.”

moḷiniṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text; from the Jātaka verse (ajjeva maṃ moḷiniṃ pāpayassu).
moḷiniṃ.example_2: Aññassa yānassa na hettha [na hatthi (pī.)] bhūmi, ajjeva maṃ moḷiniṃ pāpayassu.
moḷiniṃ.translation_2: There is no place here for any other vehicle; take me to Molini this very day.”

bilarā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form bilarā is probably a variant reading for sacarā, the reading favoured by some editions; it is ablative singular of bilara meaning 'from the hole/ant-hill'. The PEU gloss 'hole' supports this. Alternatively it may be a marginal variant without grammatical fit.
bilarā.example_1: 64. Āsīviso tāta pahūtatejo, yo taṃ adaṃsī [aḍaṃsī (syā.)] sacarā [bilarā (sī.), piḷārā (syā.), patarā (pī.)] udicca;
bilarā.translation_1: The serpent, dear one, is of great power, which bit you having risen from the ant-hill;

piḷārā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the verse (with bilarā and patarā) for the mound from which the snake rose; the meaning 'anthill' fits sacarā udicca. Uncertain analysis, possibly not a compound; treated here as a feminine ā-stem.
piḷārā.example_1: 64. Āsīviso tāta pahūtatejo, yo taṃ adaṃsī [aḍaṃsī (syā.)] sacarā [bilarā (sī.), piḷārā (syā.), patarā (pī.)] udicca;
piḷārā.translation_1: The serpent, dear one, is of great power, which bit you having risen from the ant-hill;

khamyataṃ.meaning_2: is forgiven; may be pardoned; let it be forgiven
khamyataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse taṃ khamyataṃ puttakahetu majja, khamyataṃ is best taken as the 3rd singular present of a passive/causative khamyati, 'let that be forgiven', with taṃ as its subject. The PEU entry suggests khamayatu or an imperative 'let him be patient'. The form looks passive; the reading is uncertain. Majja is probably majjha, 'for me'.
khamyataṃ.example_2: 71. Maṇḍabya bhāsiṃ yamabhāsaneyyaṃ [bhāsissaṃ abhāsaneyyaṃ (sī. syā. pī.), bhāsissa ’ mabhāsaneyyaṃ (?)], taṃ khamyataṃ puttakahetu majja;
khamyataṃ.translation_2: Maṇḍabya, I have spoken what should not be said; may it be forgiven today for the sake of the son;

akataññuna.meaning_2: ungrateful; not knowing the kindness done (to oneself)
akataññuna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular of akataññū agreeing with dummatinā and dubbhinā in these verses. Literally "not knowing what was done", i.e. ungrateful.
akataññuna.translation_2: Such is the wretched one, the fool, the ungrateful and treacherous one;

labbhitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text labbhitā is nominative singular feminine agreeing with iddhī. The form is a past participle of the passive labbhati. The PEU entry suggests labhita, but labbhitā is the reading here.
labbhitā.example_2: Tayāmā labbhitā iddhī, ettha me natthi saṃsayo.
labbhitā.translation_2: By you this power was obtained; here I have no doubt.

kaḷambāni.meaning_2: shoot sprouting from a palm nut; kind of edible plant; (according to commentary) bulbous plant
kaḷambāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text kaḷambāni is nominative plural neuter, listed among plants that are not present. The form is sometimes written as kaḷambāni with a retroflex ḷ. DPD: probably related to kaḍamba.
kaḷambāni.example_2: 82. Na takkalā santi na āluvāni [ālupāni (sī. syā. pī.)], na biḷāliyo na kaḷambāni tāta;
kaḷambāni.translation_2: No bulbs are here, no herbs for cooking meet, no catmint, nor no other plant to eat, dear.

paṭilacchase.meaning_2: will get; will receive; will obtain; will acquire
paṭilacchase.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person singular future of paṭilabhati, with the ending -ssase (cf. Sanskrit -syase). The form occurs in the verse mayāpi tāta paṭilacchase tuvaṃ, 'you too, dear, will receive'. The future here may carry a sense of consequence or destiny.
paṭilacchase.example_2: Mayāpi tāta paṭilacchase tuvaṃ, etādisaṃ kamma jarūpanīto;
paṭilacchase.translation_2: You too, dear, will receive such kamma when you are old;

vārayituṃ.meaning_2: to prevent; to restrain; to ward off; to turn away
vārayituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of the causative vārayati. In the text it depends on arahāmi and ussahe; the object is kumāraṃ or no.

niddhāmase.meaning_2: we expel; we drive out; we remove
niddhāmase.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading niddhāmase (1st person plural, causative/ desiderative?) for niddhāpaye, meaning 'let us expel'. The form is 1st plural with -āmase ending. Root √dham with prefix ni and causative sign *e.
niddhāmase.example_1: Niddhāpaye [niddhāmase (pī.)] tañca sakā agārā, aññampi te sā dukhamāvaheyya.
niddhāmase.translation_1: Let us expel her from our house, for she might bring other suffering upon you as well.

dāsso.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Alternative form dāsyo in the text; dāsso is a variant reading. Nominative plural.
dāsso.example_1: 101. Dāsā ca dāsyo [dāsso (sī. pī.), dāsī (syā.)] anujīvino ca, paricārakā kammakarā ca sabbe;
dāsso.translation_1: Male slaves and female slaves, those dependent on us, followers, and workers, all of them;

nāsīde.meaning_2: does not associate (with); does not keep company (with); does not sit near
nāsīde.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Na + asīdati (aor of √sad). 3rd singular present, active. The line mixes present and aorist; possibly nāsīde = na + āsīde (ā + √sad, optative).
nāsīde.translation_2: One should not associate with such worthless people in whom there is no gratitude.

abbhuḷhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text abbhuḷhaṃ is a variant reading for abbahī (aorist 3rd singular). The form appears here in the verse as abbhuḷhaṃ, which agrees with the causative-like sense 'extracted'; the related reading abbuhi is also given. Root is √hā 1: hā → hī → hi → ahī.
abbhuḷhaṃ.example_1: 123. Abbahī [abbuhi (syā.), abbhuḷhaṃ (ka.)] vata me sallaṃ, yamāsi hadayassitaṃ [sokaṃ hadayanissitaṃ (vi. va.1215)];
abbhuḷhaṃ.translation_1: You have extracted the dart lodged in my heart,

loṇiyateliyaṃ.meaning_2: prepared with salt and oil; sprinkled with salt and oil; seasoned with salt and oil
loṇiyateliyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of loṇiya (salty; with salt) and teliya (with oil; oily). In the verses it describes village food; accusative singular agreeing with an understood object. PEU treats it as a bahubbīhi adjective.
loṇiyateliyaṃ.translation_2: For I, too, friend, eat food in the village prepared with salt and oil.

ghasasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text ghasasī is 2nd singular present with the emphatic -i (ghasasi + i), addressed to the bird in the Jātaka verse. PEU splits it as ghasa + a + si.
ghasasī.example_2: Utrasto ghasasī bhīto, tena vaṇṇo tavediso.
ghasasī.translation_2: You eat in fear and trembling; that is why your colour is like that.

maṃmiva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of maṃ (accusative of ahaṃ) + iva. In the text it modifies piyo: 'beloved like me'.
maṃmiva.example_2: Ahiṃsāya cara loke, piyo hohisi maṃmiva.
maṃmiva.translation_2: Walk in the world harming no one, and you will be beloved like me.

sīri.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text sīri is a variant spelling of siri. Nominative singular, coordinated with dhitī and matī.
sīri.example_1: yā tādisī sīri dhitī matī ca;
sīri.example_2: 145. Saccaṃ kira tvaṃ api [tvampi (sī.), tuvampi (syā.), tvaṃ asi (ka.)] bhūripañña, yā tādisī sīri dhitī matī ca;
sīri.translation_2: “Is it true, O you of vast wisdom, that you possess such glory, steadfastness, and intelligence;

tāyatebhāvavasūpanitaṃ.meaning_2: does not protect; not protected from the state of existence
tāyatebhāvavasūpanitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound word with sandhi in a verse; na tāyate bhāvavasa-upanitaṃ: 'is not protected from the power of existence'. Uncertain segmentation; possibly tāyate + bhāva + vasa + upanitaṃ.
tāyatebhāvavasūpanitaṃ.example_2: Na tāyatebhāvavasūpanitaṃ, yo yavakaṃ bhuñjasi appasūpaṃ.
tāyatebhāvavasūpanitaṃ.translation_2: and yet you do not protect [yourself] from what is brought by the state of existence, while you eat barley with little broth?”

abhijīhanāya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in the Jātaka verse (Jā 147) meaning the time for effort/advancing. Dative singular in the text. The PEU splits as abhi + jeha + yu; the root is √ji with an irregular jīh base.
abhijīhanāya.example_2: 147. Kālañca ñatvā abhijīhanāya, mantehi atthaṃ paripācayitvā;
abhijīhanāya.translation_2: Having known the time for advancing, and having ripened the welfare with wise counsel,

paripācayitvā.meaning_2: having matured; having ripened; having brought to fulfilment
paripācayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā from the causative paripācayati. Possibly written for paripācetvā; the meaning is the same. In the verse, mantehi atthaṃ paripācayitvā means 'having brought the matter to maturity by counsel'.
paripācayitvā.example_2: 147. Kālañca ñatvā abhijīhanāya, mantehi atthaṃ paripācayitvā;
paripācayitvā.translation_2: Having known the time for advancing, and having ripened the welfare with wise counsel,

sukhīpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sukhī (nominative singular of sukhī, 'happy') + pi (emphatic 'too, even'). The commentary suggests alternative splits: sukhī hi eke and sukhīti heke. Subject of karonti in the verse.
sukhīpi.example_2: 148. Sukhīpi heke [sukhī hi eke (sī.), sukhīti heke (?)] na karonti pāpaṃ, avaṇṇasaṃsaggabhayā puneke;
sukhīpi.translation_2: “Some, though happy, do not do evil; others do not through fear of association with the lowly.

koliniyā.meaning_2: of good family; of noble lineage; well-born
koliniyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Attributive adjective describing a wife; here in the feminine, instrumental singular (koliniyā) agreeing with sīlavatī. Alternatively analysed as kola + iya (PEU gives kulina + iya).
koliniyā.example_2: Koliniyā sīlavatī patibbatā, dāresu ve sotthānaṃ tadāhu.
koliniyā.translation_2: Of good lineage, virtuous, and faithful—that, they say, is safety in wives.

sattaha.meaning_2: seven days; week; name of a king
sattaha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi in the text for sattāho, nominative singular, in a list of kings' names. Also a common noun meaning 'seven days'; the commentary may explain it as a proper name.
sattaha.example_2: Daḷha kaṇha dhanañjaya saṅkhavaro, raja sattaha kassa ca [sattāhasasākha (syā.)] takkalinā;
sattaha.translation_2: Daḷha, Kanha, Dhanañjaya, Saṅkhavara, Rāja, Sattāha, and the Kassa [Sattāhasasākha] and Takkalin,

subhūrisa.meaning_2: name of a bird; name of a goose
subhūrisa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed as a proper name in the verse, along with cakkavāka; probably a kind of bird. The compound is not fully analysable: su + bhūri + isa? Doubtful.
subhūrisa.example_2: Dhammaṃ kukkuṭa kuṇḍali bhojanadā, cakkavāka subhūrisa sotthi ghaṭoti.
subhūrisa.translation_2: Dhamma, Kukkuṭa, Kuṇḍali, Bhojanadā, Cakkavāka, Subhūrisa, Sotthi, and Ghaṭa.
